sources.entry: Lighttpd - Secure, fast, compliant, and very flexible web server that has been optimized for high-performance environments. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause C/deb/Docker

summary.name: lighttpd
summary.one_liner: lighttpd is a secure, fast, and flexible open source web server optimized for high-performance environments with low resource use.
use_cases: running a high-traffic web server with low resources
hardening TLS configuration on a web server
summary.what_it_does: lighttpd is a web server that uses memory and CPU efficiently and claims lower resource use than other popular web servers. It supports FastCGI, CGI, authentication, output compression, and URL rewriting. The page is a news/changelog section describing recent default changes: TLS minimum protocol moving to TLSv1.3, TLSv1.3 groups limited to a recommended set, h2c upgrade disabled by default, and a hardened systemd service unit. It also explains that server.error-handler-404 now only handles 404 responses and points to server.error-handler and mod_magnet for dynamic error pages.
notable: Released under the open source revised BSD license
TLSv1.3 is now the default minimum TLS protocol
Hardened systemd lighttpd.service unit that may need admin overrides on some distros
Config split into lighttpd.annotated.conf and a simpler lighttpd.conf header
caveats: Hardened systemd service may need admin overrides on non-typical systems that run lighttpd as root or run CGI scripts as root
server.error-handler-404 no longer applies to 403 responses
Packagers must include the renamed config files in their packaging scripts
